title: Contagious: Why Things Catch On
author: Jonah Berger
edition_analyzed: First edition, published by Simon & Schuster
target_audience: Students and researchers in marketing, business, and psychology
General readers interested in human behavior and trends
core_themes: Word of mouth and social transmission
How ideas, products, and behaviors spread
Using social influence to make information contagious
primary_purpose: To explain why certain products, ideas, and behaviors catch on and become popular, revealing the underlying principles that drive things to go viral and providing actionable strategies for making ideas and products more shareable.

structure_format.organization: Introduction and six core chapters based on the STEPPS framework, with concrete examples and case studies throughout
features: STEPPS framework (Social Currency, Triggers, Emotion, Public, Practical Value, Stories)

key_concepts_lessons: Virality is driven less by advertising and more by word of mouth and social influence.
Six key STEPPS principles—Social Currency, Triggers, Emotion, Public, Practical Value, Stories—make things more likely to be shared.
People share things that make them look good (Social Currency).
Ideas linked to frequent triggers in the environment are remembered and discussed more often.
Emotionally evocative content is more shared, especially content that arouses high-arousal emotions.
Visibility in public spaces helps products and ideas catch on (Public).
Useful, valuable information gets shared as a form of helping others (Practical Value).
Narratives (Stories) serve as vessels that carry ideas to others.
style_tone: Storytelling with a mix of research and anecdote
notable_features: Encourages strategic rather than accidental word of mouth
Blends psychology, business, and marketing research with memorable stories
Frequently cited across marketing, social media, and business strategy communities
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2010s during the rise of social media platforms and increased focus on viral marketing, the book reflects greater interest in understanding how ideas spread organically in a digitally connected world.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller and widely used resource in marketing and business education
Praised for its clear framework and actionable advice
Influential among marketing professionals, entrepreneurs, and content creators
Some critics note that some examples are more memorable than scientific, and virality can't always be engineered
comparable_titles: Made to Stick by Chip Heath and Dan Heath
The Tipping Point by Malcolm Gladwell
Talk Triggers by Jay Baer and Daniel Lemin
